messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Coordination: model deprecation notice & customer exception flow (publication latch)

Team —

TL;DR: We need to lock a comms publication plan for the October->November model family deprecation, define the customer exception (exemption) intake & review process, and confirm who owns the ‘publication latch’ (i.e., the gating decision that prevents notices from going live until all engineering & security checks are green).

Asks:
- Marissa: draft timeline for customer notice, emails, and portal banner. Target publish week: 11/02. Can you confirm slack cadence for announcement to sales/CS?
- Irene: tech constraints — what hard blockers exist for listing recommended migration variants, sequencing for traffic-shift opt-ins, and visible SDK deprecation headers?
- Ben: ops readiness — who owns rollback hatch, pager coverage for the week of publication, and a quick playbook if we get >3 critical tickets in 24h?
- Naomi: comms copy — I attached a short outline. Please produce a 1-page customer-facing FAQ + snippet for Sales one-pager by Thursday.

We also need to finalize the exception flow: intake form, required evidence, SLA for review (48h standard), and escalation to the Exceptions Board for non-standard asks. I propose a simple two-tier approach: auto-approve short-term (<=30 days) infra-only exemptions, board review for anything longer or feature-impacting.

I'll coordinate a 30-min sync tomorrow to lock owners unless you have objections.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Product Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Coordination: model deprecation notice & customer exception flow (publication latch)

Alex / team —

Notes from infra/security side:
- Migration variants: We can publish recommended model mappings immediately, but we cannot guarantee identical tokenization/response parity for some finetuned variants. Need a clear ‘behavior delta’ note in the FAQ.
- SDK headers: We can add `x-rw-deprecation-warning` header in the next SDK patch; timeline 10/30 for client libraries.
- Canary gating: We require 48h of canary traffic with metric thresholds (latency p95, error rate <0.1%) and a negative-regression run on 200 prompt samples. If those pass, SRE will signal green.
- Exceptions: For infra-only exemptions (e.g., pinned model instance requests), we can auto-approve at infra level if resource commitments are acceptable. For product/behavior exemptions (customers who rely on output quirks), require exceptions board review with evidence (prompt sets + regression eval).

I will create the regression harness JIRA and share the link. We need the evaluation prompt set from Product by EOD Wed (10/21).

— Irene
Irene Choi
Staff Engineer, Reliability & Security
Redwood Inference

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the heads up. Acme depends on the legacy v1-stable endpoint for a mixed critical/experimental workload. Two asks: 1) If we submit an exception request, can you confirm expected SLA for review and an emergency 90-day temporary pin while we validate migration, and 2) will you provide example prompt/eval templates so we can prepare the evidence you mentioned?

We would like the 90-day pin if possible; moving that workload touches three product teams on our side and requires a dedicated migration sprint.

Happy to jump on a short call with your team tomorrow.

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Coordination: model deprecation notice & customer exception flow (publication latch)

Sarah — thanks for the quick reply and context.

Short answer: yes, we support a documented exception intake and will evaluate a 90-day temporary pin on a case-by-case basis. Here's the immediate plan and next steps:

1) Intake artifacts: we need (a) short business justification, (b) regression prompt set (20–50 samples) with expected outputs, (c) infra plan (GPU/throughput requirements), and (d) target cutover date. I attached an `exception_evidence_template.xlsx` to the thread.
2) SLA: standard review target is 48h; for high-impact customers (enterprise accounts + procurement loop) we'll escalate to the Exceptions Board and target 24–72h.
3) Temporary pins: we will not auto-grant >30 days without board approval. For Acme, given the scale, I'll escalate to the board for a 90-day temporary pin contingent on (i) receiving the artifacts above by 10/26 and (ii) an agreed migration plan with milestones.
4) Comms & publication latch: Product (me) will own the final ‘publish’ approval with sign-off checklist items from SRE (Irene) and Comms (Naomi / Marissa). If Acme submits evidence and we board-approve, we will add an exception note to the customer email and portal banner.

Naomi / Marissa: Naomi — can you prep the small FAQ addition around exceptions (template language + what we’ll say in the email) so we can ship the notice without blocking Acme’s request?

Ben: please confirm ops readiness for the week of 11/02 and the rollback playbook.

Irene: please create the regression harness JIRA and post the link back into this thread when ready.

I will schedule a 30-min exception-triage slot on Monday 10/26 10:00 PT to review any incoming artifacts; invite forthcoming.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Product Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachment: exception_evidence_template.xlsx (template for intake)
